job.title: Plant Fitter
job.description:
Our client, a leading manufacturer of heavy equipment, is seeking an experienced Plant Fitter / Heavy Plant Mechanic to join their team in Co. Laois.

This is a full-time, workshop-based role focused on the mechanical assembly, fitting and commissioning of heavy plant and equipment, with a strong emphasis on hydraulic systems.

The role would suit candidates from plant, agricultural, quarry, construction or heavy engineering backgrounds who have strong hands-on mechanical and hydraulic experience. Full training will be provided on company-specific equipment and systems.

What You Will Do

  • Carry out mechanical fitting and assembly of heavy plant and equipment
  • Install and connect hydraulic systems, components and pipework
  • Read and interpret hydraulic and electrical schematics
  • Carry out hydraulic plumbing and system installation
  • Diagnose and resolve mechanical, hydraulic and electrical faults
  • Assist with the testing and commissioning of completed equipment
  • Operate overhead cranes, forklifts and hand tools
  • Ensure all work meets required Health & Safety and quality standards
  • Work independently and as part of a skilled production team

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience as a Plant Fitter, Plant Mechanic, Heavy Equipment Mechanic, Mechanical Fitter, Hydraulic Fitter, Agri Mechanic or similar
  • Strong hands-on mechanical fitting and maintenance experience
  • Good practical knowledge of hydraulic systems
  • Experience working with heavy plant or machinery
  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, hydraulic and electrical schematics
  • Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills
  • Good attention to detail and a strong work ethic
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive hourly rate, depending on experience
  • Overtime available
  • Performance-related bonus
  • Pension scheme
  • Temporary accommodation available
  • On-site parking
  • Canteen facilities
  • Full training on company-specific equipment and systems

Apply today for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

You may also have searched for: Plant Fitter, Plant Mechanic, Heavy Plant Mechanic, Heavy Equipment Fitter, Mechanical Fitter, Hydraulic Fitter, Agri Mechanic, Agricultural Mechanic, Construction Plant Technician.

job.title: Senior Unit Manager - Dairy ( Saudi Arabia )
job.description:
Are you looking currently looking to travel abroad and gain great experience working on a large scale dairy farm ? If so this may be the role for you.

We are now accepting cvs for positions that will be starting from January 2027 on-wards.

In return my client is offering a lucrative tax free package which will include a basic salary & bonus. Salary in year 1 (€50000 to €54000). Accommodation and food provided , 98 days annual leave , access to gym sand sports facilities and further career progression opportunities.

If you possess 3 to 4 years practical milking experience from Ireland and now seeking to work on a larger scale dairy farm we would be very interested in hearing from you.

Overview

FRS Recruitment are currently recruiting for Senior Unit Managers for a large dairy farm operation in the Middle East.Ideally my client is seeking applications from candidates whom can make a minimum commitment of 3-5 years.

My client is one of the largest vertically integrated dairy companies in the Middle East which presently has 90,000 cows and rear 70,000 young stock in 6 modern dairy farms. The successful candidates for these roles will undergo a programme of on the job training in all aspects reflecting the best European standards.

FRS Recruitment which is part of the FRS Network has been serving the Irish agricultural trade since 1980. My client is particularly interested in seeking applications from candidates with hands on milking experience from Ireland & UK. If you have gained work experience through college on large scale dairy operations outside of Ireland and UK this would be a distinct advantage.

Core purpose of the role

To maximise production and thereby profit of the farm by planning and organising all farm functional activities within assigned areas of responsibility and making the most efficient use of all resources at this disposal.

Reporting to the Farm Manager you will be responsible for the following duties

  • Calving ; calve cows & heifers , feed colostrum and do daily recordings , vaccinations and record movements per calving
  • Feeding ; feeding heifers & bull calves from day old to weaning. Cows are fed 4 times per day
  • Health ; detect sick cows and diagnose and treat them
  • Breeding ; work closely with the breeding team and select cows that are unsuitable for re breeding.
  • Milking parlour ; test milk for quality and BF % & SNF %.

Candidate profile

  • 3rd level Degree or Cert required ( Minimum of Level 7 required )
  • 3 to 4 years practical experience working on Irish dairy farm
  • Work experience in Australia or New Zealand through college placement or other is a distinct advantage.
  • Career minded and highly motivated.

Remuneration

  • Starting salary of 50000 Euros + end or year bonus ( equivalent to 1 months salary ) - all tax free
  • 6 free flights to and from Ireland to Riyadh
  • 98 days annual leave
  • Accommodation & food provided
  • Access to gyms and very modern leisure facilities.
  • Further career progression

To apply

If you possess 3 to 4 years practical milking experience from Ireland and now seeking to work on a larger scale dairy farm we would be very interested in hearing from you.

Application by cv only , please submit cv through link at the bottom of job advert.

Interested candidates can call John directly on 087 9955439

* Please note - we do not accept cvs through whatsapp*

job.title: Social Care Worker
job.description:
Discovery & Assessment of Needs Project - Social Care Worker

Location: North Dublin, with some travel to satellite locations
Duration: Approximately 8 weeks
Contract Type: Project-Based / Temporary
HSE Payscale

We are currently recruiting Social Care Workers to join a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) for an exciting Discovery and Assessment of Needs Project within an adult Disability Team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for professionals who are passionate about person-centred practice, disability rights, social inclusion and supporting people to achieve meaningful life outcomes.

The project will focus on gaining a deeper understanding of the aspirations, goals and support needs of adults who use my client's services. The findings will help inform the future development and redesign of adult services in line with the principles of New Directions, ensuring that supports remain person-centred, evidence-based and focused on individual outcomes.

The Opportunity

Successful candidates will receive structured training and induction from the CRC in the assessment methodology before commencing the project. Ongoing support will also be provided throughout the assignment.

Over approximately 8 weeks, you will undertake scheduled assessments with adults attending services.

Assessments will explore:

  • Individual aspirations, goals and future plans
  • Community participation and social inclusion
  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes
  • Unmet needs and opportunities for further development
  • Individuals' strengths, preferences and personal priorities

Requirements

  • Social Care degree
  • CORU reg
  • Irish working rights
  • Have experience working with adults with disabilities
  • Understand the principles of New Directions and rights-based service delivery
  • Have strong skills in engagement, interviewing, facilitation and information gathering
  • Can effectively engage with adults with diverse communication needs
  • Take a strengths-based and progressive approach to disability support
  • Are passionate about person-centred practice, social inclusion and empowering individuals to achieve their goals
  • Share values centred around respect, collaboration, quality and person-centred support

Interested?

If you are a qualified with relevant disability experience and would like to be considered for this project, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to find out more about this exciting short-term project opportunity.

Call Isabel 0861449043 for more information.

  • Excellent analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive, results-driven approach with strong organisational and problem-solving ability

What's On Offer?

  • €80,000 - €91,000 salary
  • Compressive benefits package including Bonus, Healthcare and Pension
  • Permanent position with a well-established industrial operation
  • Senior engineering role with significant ownership and responsibility
  • Opportunity to deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, reliability, quality and cost

A well-established Irish medical devices company with over 25 years in the market is looking for a Clinical Sales Executive to join their growing commercial team. What You'll Actually Be Doing

What You'll Need

  • Experience selling into hospital laboratories, ideally with direct exposure to histology or pathology departments
  • Background in instrumentation and diagnostics sales — you understand the equipment and the buying process
  • An existing network of contacts across Irish hospital labs and HSE procurement
  • Experience managing tender and public procurement processes
  • Full clean driving licence, comfortable covering a national territory

What's In It For You

  • Competitive base + uncapped, achievable commission
  • Company car
  • Laptop & telephone
  • Private healthcare
  • Contributory pension
  • Genuine autonomy and ownership of your territory

Why This One's Worth a Look

This is a stable, family-run business that's been performing well in this space for decades, and they're selective because they want people who deliver.

  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Senior Respiratory Physiologist to join a progressive and expanding Respiratory Physiology Department within a leading private healthcare provider in Galway.

We are seeking a highly motivated and patient-focused professional with significant experience in sleep diagnostics and respiratory physiology laboratory services. The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality diagnostic investigations while supporting the continued development of an advanced respiratory and sleep service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform and interpret a comprehensive range of respiratory physiology investigations, including spirometry, lung volumes, gas transfer (DLCO), bronchial challenge testing and overnight oximetry.
  • Lead and deliver high-quality sleep diagnostic services, including the setup, scoring and interpretation of ambulatory and laboratory-based sleep studies.
  • Demonstrate expertise in the investigation and management pathway for sleep-disordered breathing, including CPAP initiation, troubleshooting and patient education.
  • Ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the respiratory physiology and sleep laboratory, maintaining the highest standards of quality assurance and equipment calibration.
  • Work collaboratively with Respiratory Consultants, Sleep Physicians and the multidisciplinary team to provide an efficient, patient-centred diagnostic service.
  • Maintain accurate clinical records and prepare detailed technical reports.
  • Participate in service development, clinical audit and implementation of best practice.
  • Support, mentor and supervise junior physiologists and contribute to ongoing staff education and training.

Essential Requirements

  • Degree in Clinical Measurement Science, Clinical Physiology or an equivalent recognised qualification.

job.title: Accounts Payable Officer
job.description:
FRS Recruitment is delighted to be recruiting on behalf of a leading and growing construction and facilities management company operating across the Munster & Mid-West region with head office in Limerick.

Due to continued growth, our client is seeking an experienced Accounts Payable Administrator to join their finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented finance professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced, project-driven environment and wants to develop their career within a well-established organisation.

The Role

You will play a key role in managing the company's purchase ledger function, ensuring supplier payments are processed accurately and efficiently while maintaining strong financial controls.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable & Invoice Processing

  • Process, log and allocate supplier and subcontractor invoices to the correct projects and cost codes.
  • Coordinate invoice approvals with Project Managers and Quantity Surveyors.
  • Match invoices to purchase orders, delivery dockets and completion confirmations.
  • Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies relating to pricing, quantities, VAT or scope of work.
  • Maintain accurate records within the company's accounting and job-costing systems.

Supplier Payments

  • Prepare monthly supplier payment runs for management approval.
  • Process supplier invoices, payments and credit notes accurately and on time.
  • Administer early-payment requests and ensure agreed terms are correctly applied.
  • Ensure compliance with Irish VAT regulations, including reverse charge requirements where applicable.

Subcontractor Administration & Compliance

  • Support Relevant Contracts Tax (RCT) processes and payment notifications.
  • Maintain up-to-date supplier and subcontractor records, including tax clearance certificates, insurance documentation and banking details.
  • Manage new supplier onboarding and adhere to fraud-prevention controls when updating banking information.

Reconciliations & Month-End Support

  • Complete monthly supplier statement reconciliations.
  • Reconcile company credit card and fuel card accounts.
  • Prepare aged creditor reports and support month-end accrual processes.
  • Ensure project costing information remains accurate and up to date.

General Administration

  • Maintain organised electronic filing systems and financial records.
  • Act as the first point of contact for supplier queries and remittance requests.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives within the purchase-to-pay process.

Candidate Profile

Essential Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years' experience in Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger or a similar finance role.
  • Previous experience within construction, contracting, facilities management or another project-based environment is highly desirable.
  • Experience using Sage (Sage Business Cloud Accounting preferred) or a similar accounting package.
  • Strong Excel skills including lookups, filters, pivot tables and reconciliations.
  • Good understanding of Irish VAT requirements.
  • Excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments.

Desirable

  • Knowledge of Relevant Contracts Tax (RCT) and construction reverse charge VAT.
  • Experience with job-costing or purchase-order systems such as LiveCosts.
  • Accounting Technician qualification (ATI), or currently studying towards a finance qualification.
  • Experience with credit card, fuel card or expense reconciliations.
  • Previous involvement in implementing or improving purchase-order processes.

What's on Offer?

  • Pension contribution matching up to 5%.
  • 20 days annual leave plus public holidays.
  • Support for professional development and further study, including Accounting Technicians Ireland qualifications.
  • Opportunity to join a growing and successful organisation with a strong pipeline of projects across Munster.

job.title: Financial Analyst & Commercial Modelling Specialist
job.description:
We are seeking a highly analytical and commercially minded Financial Analyst & Commercial Modelling Specialist due to business growth. This is an exciting opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys translating complex financial and operational data into actionable insights that drive business performance and strategic decision-making.

Reporting to the Business Intelligence Manager, you will play a key role in supporting business growth through the development of financial models, commercial pricing solutions, tender submissions, and strategic business cases. Working closely with Commercial, Operations, HR, and Finance teams, you will ensure that pricing proposals are commercially competitive, financially robust, and aligned with organisational objectives.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex commercial challenges, and wants to make a tangible impact on business success.

A predominantly remote role with some days in the initial weeks working from a Tipperary office.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Modelling & Analysis

  • Develop, maintain, and enhance detailed financial models to support bids, tenders, business cases, and strategic projects.
  • Conduct financial forecasting, scenario planning, and sensitivity analysis to assess commercial opportunities and risks.
  • Ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of all financial modelling outputs.
  • Analyse operational and financial performance data to support strategic decision-making.

Tender Pricing & Commercial Bid Support

  • Collaborate with operational and commercial stakeholders to gather cost, resource, and pricing assumptions.
  • Develop robust pricing models that balance competitiveness, profitability, and risk.
  • Support the preparation, review, and submission of tender responses and commercial proposals.
  • Evaluate contract opportunities and renewal pricing strategies.

Commercial Insight & Profitability Analysis

  • Assess customer, contract, and service-line profitability to identify opportunities for margin improvement and cost optimisation.
  • Provide recommendations that support sustainable business growth and commercial performance.
  • Monitor financial performance against targets and identify areas for improvement.

Forecasting & Business Planning

  • Support budgeting, forecasting, and long-term planning activities through detailed financial analysis.
  • Identify financial risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.
  • Provide insights that support resource allocation and investment decisions.

Stakeholder Engagement & Decision Support

  • Partner with stakeholders across Commercial, Operations, HR, and Finance functions.
  • Present financial findings, assumptions, and recommendations to a variety of audiences.
  • Translate complex financial data into clear and commercially relevant insights.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure compliance with internal governance, approval processes, and financial controls.
  • Maintain clear documentation and audit trails for pricing models and commercial assumptions.
  • Contribute to the ongoing enhancement of modelling methodologies, pricing frameworks, and commercial processes.

Essential Requirements

  • QQI Level 8 Honours Degree (or equivalent) in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years' experience in financial analysis, commercial finance, bid pricing, tender support, or financial modelling.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis, and dashboard development.
  • Strong understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, and profitability analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex financial data into meaningful commercial insights and recommendations.
  • Strong commercial acumen with an understanding of pricing strategies and contract profitability.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a dynamic environment.
  • Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.

Desirable Qualifications & Experience

  • Professional finance qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or equivalent), or currently working towards qualification.
  • Experience supporting public or private sector tenders and procurement processes.
  • Experience using Power BI, SQL, ERP systems, or financial planning and analysis tools.
  • Experience within a contract-based, healthcare, facilities management, logistics, outsourced services, or related commercial environment.
  • Knowledge of pricing methodologies, contract costing, and commercial risk assessment.

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking organisation.
  • Play a key role in shaping commercial strategy and supporting business growth.
  • Work on high-impact projects and strategic business opportunities.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career progression.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

Apply Today

If you are passionate about financial analysis, commercial strategy, and delivering insights that drive performance, we would love to hear from you. Apply today with an updated copy of your CV to Ciara Lawler for immediate consideration.

job.title: Demand Planner- Dublin
job.description:
My client, a leading industrial parts manufacturer and distributor, is currently seeking an experienced Demand Planner to join their Supply Chain team in North Dublin.

Due to continued growth, my client is looking for an ambitious and commercially minded Demand Planner to play a key role in improving forecasting, demand planning and inventory management across the business.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a collaborative and fast-paced environment, working closely with Purchasing, Sales and Operations to improve forecast accuracy, stock availability and overall supply chain performance.

Key responsibilities for the Demand Planner will include:

  • Managing and maintaining the company's demand planning and forecasting tool.
  • Reviewing and validating forecasts and providing reporting on forecast accuracy.
  • Supporting and strengthening the company's S&OP processes.
  • Analysing sales trends and commercial information to improve forecasting accuracy and service levels.
  • Leading out-of-stock reporting and root cause analysis to minimise lost sales.
  • Identifying future inventory risks and opportunities and providing recommendations to key stakeholders.
  • Managing demand planning requirements for new product introductions, product phase-ins and phase-outs.
  • Acting as the key link between the Sales and Purchasing teams, translating commercial insights into forecast adjustments.
  • Working closely with Operations and Sales to optimise inventory levels across third-party logistics locations.
  • Developing reporting and insights to support better supply chain and purchasing decisions.

The requirements for the Demand Planner include but are not limited to:

  • A relevant third-level qualification in Supply Chain, Business or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of 3 years' experience in Demand or Production Planning
  • Strong knowledge of forecasting methodologies and demand planning tools.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.
  • Experience with reporting and analytics tools such as Power BI.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to work across Purchasing, Sales and Operations.
  • A structured, detail-oriented and process-driven approach.
  • A proactive mindset and willingness to learn and develop within the business.

If you feel that you fulfil the above requirements please apply today with your CV. If you have any further queries please contact Rachael Pando of FRS Recruitment.

job.title: Senior Radiation Therapist
job.description:
Senior Radiation Therapist

Shape the Future of Cancer Care

An exceptional opportunity has arisen for experienced Senior Radiation Therapists to join a brand-new, purpose-built cancer centre in the Midwest of Ireland.

This is more than a new role—it's a chance to be part of a pioneering team from the beginning, helping to establish one of Ireland's most modern radiotherapy services and delivering world-class care to patients.

Why Join?

As a Senior Radiation Therapist, you will play a key role in developing and delivering advanced radiotherapy services within a collaborative, patient-centred environment.

Advanced Clinical Practice

Work at the forefront of radiotherapy, with opportunities to develop expertise in:

  • Stereotactic Radiotherapy (SRT/SABR)
  • Advanced treatment planning
  • Image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT)
  • Modern radiotherapy technologies and techniques
  • Varian radiotherapy system

Career Development

Commitment to investing in people and supporting long-term career growth through:

  • Clear career progression pathways
  • Leadership and management development opportunities
  • Specialist clinical roles
  • Ongoing professional education and funded training

Research & Innovation

Become part of a service committed to advancing cancer care through:

  • Participation in national and international clinical trials
  • Research collaboration and service development
  • Opportunities to contribute to innovation and evidence-based practice
  • Support for academic development and conference participation

What's On Offer

Exceptional people deserve exceptional support.

A comprehensive package will attract the best Radiation Therapists and includes:

  • Competitive salary plus premium payments and performance pay
  • Attractive benefits package
  • Generous relocation support for successful candidates moving to the region
  • Excellent annual leave entitlement
  • Pension scheme
  • Continuous professional development funding
  • Supportive multidisciplinary working environment
  • Access to the latest radiotherapy technologies within a newly developed facility

About You

You are an experienced Radiation Therapist who is passionate about delivering outstanding patient care and eager to contribute to the development of an innovative cancer service.

You will bring:

  • Significant post-registration experience in radiation therapy
  • Strong clinical knowledge and leadership capability
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • A commitment to quality, patient safety and continuous improvement
  • Enthusiasm for innovation, education and professional development

Be Part of Something New

This is a unique opportunity to help build a new service, influence future practice and make a lasting impact on cancer care in Ireland.

If you are looking for the next step in your career—where advanced practice, research, leadership and innovation come together - we would love to hear from you.

Emma Fenton is a specialist healthcare recruiter with 20 years experience. Applications and informal contact will be treated in strictest confidence.

job.title: Finance Administrator
job.description:
Finance Administrator

Role Purpose

Reporting to the Financial Controller, the Finance Administrator will provide essential support across the day-to-day financial operations of Aoibhneas. The successful candidate will be responsible for a range of financial administration activities, including transaction processing, reconciliations, record maintenance and general finance support.

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to contribute to the effective running of the organisation’s finance function.

Flexibility in working hours may be required to meet the needs of the organisation and support the efficient operation of the finance function.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain and update accurate financial records using Sage accounting software.
  • Process accounts payable transactions and complete supplier reconciliations.
  • Prepare and monitor payment schedules, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time.
  • Record receipts and banking transactions and reconcile these against bank statements.
  • Process receipts across various income channels, complete reconciliations and prepare relevant control accounts.
  • Reconcile and post petty cash transactions.
  • Assist with employee expense tracking, verification and processing.
  • Support month-end financial procedures, including reconciliations and journal postings.
  • Assist with the preparation of monthly management accounts and ad hoc financial reports as required.
  • Provide general administrative support to the finance function.
  • Carry out any other duties as assigned by the Financial Controller.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • Third-level qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of one year’s relevant experience in a finance, accounts, bookkeeping or administrative role.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong understanding of bookkeeping principles, financial processes and accurate financial record-keeping.
  • Previous experience in accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and processing financial transactions.
  • Experience handling confidential information and maintaining accurate financial records.
  • Excellent organisational skills with a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritise effectively and manage competing workloads to meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise professionally with suppliers, colleagues and external stakeholders.
  • Strong administration and time-management skills.
  • A proactive and flexible approach, with the ability to adapt to changing priorities.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience working with financial systems and databases.
  • Experience preparing financial reports and reconciliations.
  • Previous experience within the not-for-profit or charity sector.
  • Full driving licence.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability.
  • High levels of integrity and professionalism.
  • Strong sense of dependability and accountability.
  • Strong customer service orientation.
  • Ability to work independently and demonstrate initiative.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and consistently meet deadlines.

Personal Attributes

The successful candidate will be:

  • Professional, trustworthy and committed to maintaining confidentiality and financial integrity.
  • A strong communicator who can build positive working relationships with colleagues, suppliers and external stakeholders.
  • Highly organised, accurate and detail oriented.
  • Reliable, proactive and solution-focused, with a positive approach to their work.
  • Comfortable working independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment.
  • An effective time manager who can balance competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Someone who demonstrates initiative, sound judgement and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Employee Benefits

Aoibhneas offers a supportive working environment with a range of benefits, including:

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two well-being days, with additional incremental days in line with length of service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).

job.title: Education & Training Officer
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Education & Training Officer to lead the development and delivery of education, training and awareness initiatives across the organisation and wider community.

Role Purpose

The Education & Training Officer will develop and deliver high-quality training and awareness programmes that promote understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women, children and young people.

The role will build knowledge and skills across Aoibhneas, partner organisations and the wider community through training, education, awareness initiatives and professional engagement. The postholder will also represent the organisation and contribute to service development and best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Education & Training

  • Develop, coordinate and deliver training for staff, volunteers, students and external stakeholders.
  • Design and maintain training materials, presentations, guidance and learning resources.
  • Deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, coercive control, risk assessment, child protection and related areas.
  • Develop annual training plans aligned with organisational priorities and legislative requirements.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain accurate training records and support compliance with mandatory learning requirements.
  • Work with managers to identify learning and development needs.

Community Awareness & Engagement

  • Deliver workshops, presentations, information sessions and awareness initiatives to schools, community groups, statutory agencies and voluntary organisations.
  • Promote understanding of domestic abuse and best practice responses within communities and professional networks.
  • Represent Aoibhneas at conferences, forums, community events and professional networks.
  • Develop accessible educational and information resources.
  • Support local and national awareness initiatives relating to domestic abuse and violence against women.

Service Development

  • Research emerging trends, evidence and best practice to inform training and programme development.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps across services and partner organisations.
  • Contribute to the development of policies, procedures and practice guidance.
  • Support specialist programmes for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and organisational learning.

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with statutory agencies, schools, colleges, community organisations and professional networks.
  • Support collaborative initiatives and referral pathways.
  • Participate in relevant interagency groups, committees and professional networks.
  • Strengthen partnership approaches to domestic abuse prevention and response.

Administration & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of training delivery, attendance and outcomes.
  • Prepare reports, statistics and evaluation data.
  • Assist with funding reports, monitoring requirements and service evaluations.
  • Maintain training databases and learning management systems where applicable.
  • Liaise with the Head of Services regarding priorities and programme development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification in Education, Training, Social Care, Community Development, Social Science, Adult Education or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three years' relevant experience in training, education, social care, community development or a related setting.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women and children.
  • Proven experience designing, delivering and evaluating training programmes.
  • Excellent facilitation, presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials and learning resources.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Excellent report-writing and data management abilities.
  • Experience working with partners and external stakeholders.
  • Full driving licence.

Desirable

  • Qualification or accreditation in training/adult education.
  • Knowledge of Children First and safeguarding requirements.
  • Experience delivering training within the domestic abuse, social care or community sector.
  • Experience of interagency working.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong self-management and emotional resilience.

Role Requirements

The role will require flexibility to work across Aoibhneas and community locations, with regular travel to educational, community and organisational settings.

Working hours will generally be five days per week between 9.00am and 6.00pm, with occasional evening or weekend work required to facilitate training, awareness events and community engagement activities.

A full driving licence is essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Education & Training Officer
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Education & Training Officer to lead the development and delivery of education, training and awareness initiatives across the organisation and wider community.

Role Purpose

The Education & Training Officer will develop and deliver high-quality training and awareness programmes that promote understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women, children and young people.

The role will build knowledge and skills across Aoibhneas, partner organisations and the wider community through training, education, awareness initiatives and professional engagement. The postholder will also represent the organisation and contribute to service development and best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Education & Training

  • Develop, coordinate and deliver training for staff, volunteers, students and external stakeholders.
  • Design and maintain training materials, presentations, guidance and learning resources.
  • Deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, coercive control, risk assessment, child protection and related areas.
  • Develop annual training plans aligned with organisational priorities and legislative requirements.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain accurate training records and support compliance with mandatory learning requirements.
  • Work with managers to identify learning and development needs.

Community Awareness & Engagement

  • Deliver workshops, presentations, information sessions and awareness initiatives to schools, community groups, statutory agencies and voluntary organisations.
  • Promote understanding of domestic abuse and best practice responses within communities and professional networks.
  • Represent Aoibhneas at conferences, forums, community events and professional networks.
  • Develop accessible educational and information resources.
  • Support local and national awareness initiatives relating to domestic abuse and violence against women.

Service Development

  • Research emerging trends, evidence and best practice to inform training and programme development.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps across services and partner organisations.
  • Contribute to the development of policies, procedures and practice guidance.
  • Support specialist programmes for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and organisational learning.

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with statutory agencies, schools, colleges, community organisations and professional networks.
  • Support collaborative initiatives and referral pathways.
  • Participate in relevant interagency groups, committees and professional networks.
  • Strengthen partnership approaches to domestic abuse prevention and response.

Administration & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of training delivery, attendance and outcomes.
  • Prepare reports, statistics and evaluation data.
  • Assist with funding reports, monitoring requirements and service evaluations.
  • Maintain training databases and learning management systems where applicable.
  • Liaise with the Head of Services regarding priorities and programme development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification in Education, Training, Social Care, Community Development, Social Science, Adult Education or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three years' relevant experience in training, education, social care, community development or a related setting.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women and children.
  • Proven experience designing, delivering and evaluating training programmes.
  • Excellent facilitation, presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials and learning resources.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Excellent report-writing and data management abilities.
  • Experience working with partners and external stakeholders.
  • Full driving licence.

Desirable

  • Qualification or accreditation in training/adult education.
  • Knowledge of Children First and safeguarding requirements.
  • Experience delivering training within the domestic abuse, social care or community sector.
  • Experience of interagency working.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong self-management and emotional resilience.

Role Requirements

The role will require flexibility to work across Aoibhneas and community locations, with regular travel to educational, community and organisational settings.

Working hours will generally be five days per week between 9.00am and 6.00pm, with occasional evening or weekend work required to facilitate training, awareness events and community engagement activities.

A full driving licence is essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: House Keeping Staff
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a reliable and hardworking Housekeeper to support the cleanliness, hygiene, safety and overall presentation of Aoibhneas premises.

Role Purpose

The Housekeeper will be responsible for maintaining a high standard of cleanliness across Aoibhneas accommodation and facilities, ensuring a safe, comfortable and welcoming environment for residents, staff and visitors.

The role will involve general cleaning, maintaining cleaning supplies, supporting room turnarounds and ensuring all assigned areas are kept clean, organised and hygienic. The successful candidate will also have a basic understanding of Health & Safety procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carry out general cleaning duties across Aoibhneas premises and locations.
  • Clean floors, rooms, windows, surfaces and other areas to a high standard.
  • Clean and sanitise bathrooms and restrooms, including replenishing supplies and emptying waste.
  • Vacuum, sweep, mop, dust and maintain assigned areas.
  • Maintain adequate stocks of cleaning products, linen and other housekeeping supplies.
  • Ensure cleaning equipment and supplies are stored safely and maintained appropriately.
  • Transport, replace and manage linen as required.
  • Assist with the cleaning and preparation of residential rooms, including changing beds and preparing accommodation for new residents.
  • Maintain high standards of hygiene, cleanliness and organisation throughout all assigned areas.
  • Follow relevant Health & Safety procedures and report any hazards or maintenance issues.
  • Carry out other housekeeping duties as required.

Person Requirements

  • Previous cleaning or housekeeping experience is desirable.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high standards.
  • Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks effectively.
  • Ability to work within set timeframes and remain calm under pressure.
  • Proactive, reliable and positive approach to work.
  • Good communication skills and the ability to interact respectfully with residents, colleagues and visitors.
  • Basic understanding of Health & Safety requirements.
  • Ability to use initiative and work with minimal supervision.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Night Support Workers
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

Role: Night Support Workers

Post: Full-Time - Permanent (Pro-rata) – 4/ 3 night rotations (8hrs) / 30-hour weekly average

Salary: €36,448 (Pro-rata) per annum

Location: North Dublin/ Finglas Based

The purpose of the job is to ensure the safety and security of the women and children residing in Domestic Abuse Support services for Women and Children, while upholding and representing the organisation’s ethos and values in all aspects of the work.

The role involves, providing practical supports, safety and security in lone working capacity at nights, weekends and bank holidays. Including, operating the 24-hour Refuge Helpline and providing emergency accommodation with emotional and practical supports to women and children experiencing domestic violence.

Essential Requirements:

  • Knowledge and understanding of Domestic Violence and issues affecting women and children experiencing domestic violence.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Liaising with Gardaí, social workers, housing bodies, and health services.

Benefits:

  • Employer Pension Contribution of 5%.
  • Annual leave 22 days inclusive of 2 wellbeing days with incremental days in line with service.

job.title: Facilities Supervisor
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Facilities Supervisor to oversee the maintenance, safety, security and operational management of Aoibhneas properties, facilities and accommodation sites.

Facilities Management

  • Oversee the day-to-day management and maintenance of Aoibhneas properties, accommodation units, offices and service locations.
  • Ensure premises are safe, secure, well maintained and fit for purpose.
  • Develop and manage preventative maintenance schedules and conduct regular site inspections.
  • Coordinate repairs, maintenance and refurbishment works.
  • Manage access control, keyholding and building security arrangements.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance, inspection, servicing and compliance records.

Health, Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with relevant Health & Safety legislation and organisational policies.
  • Conduct and review risk assessments relating to buildings, equipment and workplace activities.
  • Monitor fire safety systems, emergency lighting, alarms, extinguishers and evacuation procedures.
  • Ensure statutory inspections, certifications and servicing are completed and recorded.
  • Support emergency planning and business continuity arrangements.
  • Investigate and report facilities-related incidents, hazards, accidents and near misses.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety and continuous improvement.

Contractor & Supplier Management

  • Source, appoint and manage contractors and service providers in line with procurement requirements.
  • Monitor contractor performance, service agreements, costs and value for money.
  • Ensure contractors comply with Health & Safety, safeguarding and organisational requirements.
  • Obtain quotations and support facilities-related procurement.
  • Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, landlords, maintenance providers and utility companies.

Asset & Resource Management

  • Maintain an accurate asset register across all sites.
  • Oversee furniture, equipment, fixtures and operational supplies.
  • Plan asset and equipment replacement programmes.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and monitoring of facilities expenditure.
  • Ensure effective use of facilities resources and budgets.

Projects & Administration

  • Support refurbishment, relocation, property acquisition and capital improvement projects.
  • Liaise with internal teams, contractors, consultants and regulatory bodies.
  • Monitor project timelines, budgets and deliverables.
  • Maintain accurate facilities records, policies, procedures and compliance documentation.
  • Prepare reports for management on facilities performance, compliance and risks.
  • Support inspections, audits and information requests.
  • Maintain effective systems for logging and monitoring maintenance requests.

Leadership & Support

  • Provide guidance and supervision to facilities, maintenance and contracted personnel as required.
  • Support managers in resolving facilities-related issues.
  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across teams and locations.
  • Contribute to organisational planning and service development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Relevant third-level qualification in Facilities Management, Property Management, Building Services, Health & Safety, Construction Management or a related discipline, or significant equivalent experience.
  • Minimum three years’ experience in facilities, property or operational management.
  • Experience managing multiple sites and competing priorities.
  • Strong knowledge of Health & Safety legislation and compliance requirements.
  • Experience managing contractors, service providers and maintenance programmes.
  • Strong organisational, planning and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience monitoring budgets and managing resources.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and electronic record management systems.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound operational decisions.

Desirable

  • Health & Safety qualification.
  • Facilities Management qualification.
  • Experience in the community, social care, housing or not-for-profit sector.
  • Project management experience.
  • Experience overseeing refurbishment or capital projects.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.

Role Requirements

The role requires regular travel between Aoibhneas properties and service locations, with the ability to manage competing operational priorities across multiple sites.

Working hours will generally be Monday to Friday; however, flexibility is required to respond to urgent maintenance, compliance or operational matters when necessary.

A full clean driving licence and access to transport are essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Receptionist
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Receptionist to provide high-quality reception, administrative and operational support across the organisation.

Role Purpose

The Administrator / Receptionist will be the first point of contact for visitors, service users, stakeholders and partner agencies, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient service.

The role will support the smooth day-to-day operation of Aoibhneas through reception and office administration, record management, data entry, facilities coordination and stakeholder communication, while maintaining high standards of confidentiality, professionalism and safeguarding.

Key Responsibilities

Reception & Front of House

  • Act as the first point of contact for visitors, clients, stakeholders and external agencies.
  • Manage incoming calls, emails and correspondence, directing enquiries appropriately.
  • Welcome visitors and ensure safeguarding, security and visitor procedures are followed.
  • Maintain reception, meeting rooms and public areas to a professional standard.
  • Manage incoming and outgoing post, deliveries and courier services.
  • Provide information and assistance in a professional, respectful and sensitive manner.

Administration

  • Provide administrative support to the CEO, Head of Services and managers as required.
  • Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, agendas and other documentation.
  • Maintain accurate electronic and paper filing systems.
  • Manage data entry, document control and record-keeping.
  • Maintain databases and support reporting requirements.
  • Coordinate meetings, room bookings and diaries.
  • Record meeting notes and assist with minutes where required.
  • Support managers with reports, audits and monitoring returns.

Office & Operational Support

  • Order office supplies and monitor stock levels across organisational locations.
  • Liaise with suppliers, contractors and service providers.
  • Support facilities-related requests, including maintenance, repairs and equipment servicing.
  • Assist with Health & Safety administration and compliance documentation.
  • Support procurement activities and value-for-money purchasing.

Information Management & GDPR

  • Maintain accurate, secure and up-to-date records.
  • Support compliance with GDPR, confidentiality requirements and organisational policies.
  • Handle sensitive information appropriately and maintain the confidentiality of service users and stakeholders.
  • Support the management of organisational databases and reporting systems.

Stakeholder & Service Support

  • Build positive working relationships with service users, staff, service providers, funders, contractors and community partners.
  • Assist with the coordination of meetings, events, training and organisational activities.
  • Support effective communication and information sharing across the organisation.
  • Assist service teams with data collection, monitoring and reporting.
  • Support staff with administrative requirements relating to service delivery.
  • Assist with onboarding, document management and organisational projects.

Other Duties

  • Participate in relevant training and professional development.
  • Work collaboratively across all departments and service teams.
  • Ensure organisational policies, procedures and legislative requirements are followed.
  • Work under the direction of the CEO, Head of Services or designated officer.
  • Undertake other duties appropriate to the role as required.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Qualification in Administration, Office Administration, Reception, Public Administration or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Minimum two years' experience in an administrative, reception or customer-facing role.
  • Excellent organisational and administrative skills.
  • Strong planning, time-management and multitasking abilities.
  • Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft Office and database systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to prioritise workload and meet deadlines.

Desirable

  • Experience within a social care, community, charity or not-for-profit environment.
  • Experience using CRM or case management systems.
  • Experience supporting governance, compliance or reporting processes.
  • Experience coordinating suppliers and contractors.
  • Experience supporting office or facilities management.
  • Experience in report writing and data management.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong problem-solving skills.

Role Requirements

Working hours will generally be Monday to Friday, five days per week. Flexibility may be required to support organisational events, meetings and service requirements.

The postholder may also be required to work across different Aoibhneas locations from time to time.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Finance Administrator
job.description:
FRS is proud to partner with Aoibhneas on this recruitment campaign and welcomes applications from candidates who are passionate about delivering high-quality financial administration within a values-led organisation

Role Purpose

Reporting to the Financial Controller, the Finance Administrator will provide essential support across the day-to-day financial operations of Aoibhneas. The successful candidate will be responsible for a range of financial administration activities, including transaction processing, reconciliations, record maintenance and general finance support.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate financial records using Sage.
  • Process accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and payment schedules.
  • Record and reconcile receipts, banking and petty cash transactions.
  • Process income receipts and maintain relevant control accounts.
  • Assist with employee expenses, month-end reconciliations and journal postings.
  • Support the preparation of monthly management accounts and financial reports.
  • Provide general administrative support to the finance team.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Financial Controller.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • Third-level qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of one year’s relevant experience in a finance, accounts, bookkeeping or administrative role.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong understanding of bookkeeping principles, financial processes and accurate financial record-keeping.
  • Previous experience in accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and processing financial transactions.
  • Experience handling confidential information and maintaining accurate financial records.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritise effectively and manage competing workloads to meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise professionally with suppliers, colleagues and external stakeholders.
  • Strong administration and time-management skills.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience working with financial systems and databases.
  • Experience preparing financial reports and reconciliations.
  • Previous experience within the not-for-profit or charity sector.
  • Full driving licence.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability.
  • High levels of integrity and professionalism.

Employee Benefits

Aoibhneas offers a supportive working environment with a range of benefits, including:

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two well-being days, with additional incremental days in line with length of service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).

job.title: Area Manager
job.description:
Area Manager - (For Wexford/Waterford/Kilkenny)

Our client, a large grocery chain, is looking for an Area Manager to join their well-established team and assist them with managing the stores in this area.

We are looking for strong retail professionals who have gained proven experience in a similar role. The ideal candidate would be strategic-thinking, problem-solving managers who can inspire everyone to be high achievers. Suppose you think that you have got it. In that case, you will get loads back, fast-tracked with a great package and every opportunity to develop your management abilities in a visible role with a keep-it-simple, fast-growing, retail-changing business.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead and manage a district, overseeing all Store Managers

  • Foster a positive, high-performing team environment

  • Coach, support, and develop Store Managers to drive success

  • Monitor and optimise stock flow and cash management

  • Conduct regular district tours with the Sales Executive

  • Provide analysis and feedback to support key projects

  • Manage store openings, refurbishments, and re-openings

  • Develop and execute annual business plans and staffing strategies

  • Define and track KPIs to ensure operational excellence

Requirements

  • A minimum 2.1 degree in any discipline or at least 3 years of management experience

  • Strong communication, planning, organisational, and analytical skills

  • A full, clean driving licence

  • A motivated, flexible, and results-driven leader

  • Experience in a fast-paced, dynamic environment

  • Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop teams

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary package

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave, Marriage Leave, and access to the Employee Assistance Programme

job.title: Housekeeping Staff - Part time
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a reliable and hardworking Housekeeper to support the cleanliness, hygiene, safety and overall presentation of Aoibhneas premises. This role is a part time role for 20 hours.

Role Purpose

The Housekeeper will be responsible for maintaining a high standard of cleanliness across Aoibhneas accommodation and facilities, ensuring a safe, comfortable and welcoming environment for residents, staff and visitors.

The role will involve general cleaning, maintaining cleaning supplies, supporting room turnarounds and ensuring all assigned areas are kept clean, organised and hygienic. The successful candidate will also have a basic understanding of Health & Safety procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carry out general cleaning duties across Aoibhneas premises and locations.
  • Clean floors, rooms, windows, surfaces and other areas to a high standard.
  • Clean and sanitise bathrooms and restrooms, including replenishing supplies and emptying waste.
  • Vacuum, sweep, mop, dust and maintain assigned areas.
  • Maintain adequate stocks of cleaning products, linen and other housekeeping supplies.
  • Ensure cleaning equipment and supplies are stored safely and maintained appropriately.
  • Transport, replace and manage linen as required.
  • Assist with the cleaning and preparation of residential rooms, including changing beds and preparing accommodation for new residents.
  • Maintain high standards of hygiene, cleanliness and organisation throughout all assigned areas.
  • Follow relevant Health & Safety procedures and report any hazards or maintenance issues.
  • Carry out other housekeeping duties as required.

Person Requirements

  • Previous cleaning or housekeeping experience is desirable.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high standards.
  • Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks effectively.
  • Ability to work within set timeframes and remain calm under pressure.
  • Proactive, reliable and positive approach to work.
  • Good communication skills and the ability to interact respectfully with residents, colleagues and visitors.
  • Basic understanding of Health & Safety requirements.
  • Ability to use initiative and work with minimal supervision.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: HR Administrator
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

The HR Administrator will play an important role in supporting the HR Coordinator in the effective delivery of HR services across Aoibhneas locations. This is a varied role, providing administrative support across the full employee life cycle and helping to ensure that HR processes are delivered efficiently, accurately, and in line with organisational policies, employment legislation, GDPR requirements, and best practice.

The successful candidate will have excellent organisational and administrative skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide day-to-day HR administrative support across the full employee life cycle.
  • Support the implementation, maintenance, and ongoing development of the organisation's HR Information System (HRIS), ensuring employee records are accurate and up to date.
  • Maintain employee information, contracts, personnel files, and HR databases in accordance with GDPR requirements and organisational policies.
  • Assist with the review and development of HR systems, processes, policies, and procedures, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and the employee experience.
  • Act as a point of contact for HR-related queries, providing appropriate guidance and support to employees and managers.
  • Coordinate recruitment administration, including vacancy advertising, interview scheduling, candidate correspondence, reference checks, and on boarding documentation.
  • Support on boarding, induction, probation review processes, and employee off boarding, including the coordination of exit interviews.
  • Assist with the administration and coordination of employee benefits, the Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), and employee well-being initiatives.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, including employee surveys, staff events, and internal communications, in collaboration with the Communications Officer.
  • Maintain HR compliance records and support adherence to employment legislation, organisational policies, and best practice.
  • Assist the HR Coordinator with the preparation of HR reports, metrics, and management information.
  • Coordinate mandatory training, maintain accurate training records, and assist with the development and distribution of training materials.
  • Support performance management processes, including probation reviews, performance appraisals, and learning and development initiatives.
  • Provide administrative support in relation to employee relations matters, ensuring accurate documentation and strict confidentiality at all times.
  • Update the staff intranet as required.
  • Ensure all HR administration is completed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with GDPR and confidentiality requirements.
  • Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role as reasonably requested by the HR Coordinator, Head of Services, or CEO.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • A relevant third-level qualification in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Employment Studies, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • A minimum of one year's experience in an HR administration or HR support role.
  • Demonstrable experience supporting key HR functions.
  • Working knowledge of Irish employment legislation and HR best practice.
  • Excellent administrative, organisational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage professionally and confidently with employees, managers, and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when maintaining records and preparing HR documentation.
  • A strong understanding of confidentiality, GDPR, and the importance of handling sensitive employee information.

Desirable Criteria

  • Previous experience working within the not-for-profit, charity, social care, or community sector.
  • Experience using HR Information Systems, particularly Sage HR and/or BrightHR.
  • Experience supporting recruitment campaigns, interviews, and candidate on boarding.
  • Knowledge of Garda Vetting, compliance monitoring, and employee file audits.
  • Experience assisting with payroll preparation and benefits administration.
  • Experience supporting HR projects and employee engagement initiatives.
  • A full, clean driving licence and access to transport to facilitate occasional travel between locations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, while also contributing effectively as part of a wider team.

Employee Benefits

  • Employer pension contribution of 5%.
  • 22 days' annual leave, including two well-being days, with incremental additional days in line with service.

job.title: HR Administrator
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

The HR Administrator will play an important role in supporting the HR Coordinator in the effective delivery of HR services across Aoibhneas locations. This is a varied role, providing administrative support across the full employee life cycle and helping to ensure that HR processes are delivered efficiently, accurately, and in line with organisational policies, employment legislation, GDPR requirements, and best practice.

The successful candidate will have excellent organisational and administrative skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide day-to-day HR administrative support across the full employee life cycle.
  • Support the implementation, maintenance, and ongoing development of the organisation's HR Information System (HRIS), ensuring employee records are accurate and up to date.
  • Maintain employee information, contracts, personnel files, and HR databases in accordance with GDPR requirements and organisational policies.
  • Assist with the review and development of HR systems, processes, policies, and procedures, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and the employee experience.
  • Act as a point of contact for HR-related queries, providing appropriate guidance and support to employees and managers.
  • Coordinate recruitment administration, including vacancy advertising, interview scheduling, candidate correspondence, reference checks, and on boarding documentation.
  • Support on boarding, induction, probation review processes, and employee off boarding, including the coordination of exit interviews.
  • Assist with the administration and coordination of employee benefits, the Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), and employee well-being initiatives.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, including employee surveys, staff events, and internal communications, in collaboration with the Communications Officer.
  • Maintain HR compliance records and support adherence to employment legislation, organisational policies, and best practice.
  • Assist the HR Coordinator with the preparation of HR reports, metrics, and management information.
  • Coordinate mandatory training, maintain accurate training records, and assist with the development and distribution of training materials.
  • Support performance management processes, including probation reviews, performance appraisals, and learning and development initiatives.
  • Provide administrative support in relation to employee relations matters, ensuring accurate documentation and strict confidentiality at all times.
  • Update the staff intranet as required.
  • Ensure all HR administration is completed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with GDPR and confidentiality requirements.
  • Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role as reasonably requested by the HR Coordinator, Head of Services, or CEO.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • A relevant third-level qualification in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Employment Studies, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • A minimum of one year's experience in an HR administration or HR support role.
  • Demonstrable experience supporting key HR functions.
  • Working knowledge of Irish employment legislation and HR best practice.
  • Excellent administrative, organisational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage professionally and confidently with employees, managers, and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when maintaining records and preparing HR documentation.
  • A strong understanding of confidentiality, GDPR, and the importance of handling sensitive employee information.

Desirable Criteria

  • Previous experience working within the not-for-profit, charity, social care, or community sector.
  • Experience using HR Information Systems, particularly Sage HR and/or BrightHR.
  • Experience supporting recruitment campaigns, interviews, and candidate on boarding.
  • Knowledge of Garda Vetting, compliance monitoring, and employee file audits.
  • Experience assisting with payroll preparation and benefits administration.
  • Experience supporting HR projects and employee engagement initiatives.
  • A full, clean driving licence and access to transport to facilitate occasional travel between locations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, while also contributing effectively as part of a wider team.

Employee Benefits

  • Employer pension contribution of 5%.
  • 22 days' annual leave, including two well-being days, with incremental additional days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to external supervision and an Employee Assistance Programme.

All offers of employment with Aoibhneas are subject to Garda Vetting, satisfactory reference checks, and verification of legal eligibility to work in Ireland. Aoibhneas is an equal opportunities employer. A panel may be formed from this recruitment process.

The Role

You will take a commercially focused approach to the finance function, with responsibility for:

  • Preparing monthly management accounts and management reports

  • Cash-flow forecasting, budgeting and re-forecasting
  • Project profitability and cost-to-complete reporting

  • Month-end management and reporting

job.title: EHS Coordinator
job.description:
Are you an experienced EHS Coordinator with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience looking for your next opportunity in Cork?

Our client, a well-established manufacturing company based in Little Island, Cork, is seeking an EHS Coordinator to join their EHS team. Reporting to the EHS Manager, this is a key site-based role with a particular focus on managing third-party contractors and ensuring safe, compliant execution of works on site.

What you will be doing:

  • Managing and issuing Safe Work Permits / Permit to Work for maintenance, contractor and project activities.
  • Coordinating and monitoring third-party contractors to ensure full compliance with site EHS requirements.
  • Reviewing method statements, risk assessments and safe systems of work before work commences.
  • Ensuring contractors adhere to PPE requirements, site procedures and controls for life-critical activities.
  • Supporting safety investigations, incident reporting and the implementation of corrective actions.
  • Monitoring EHS performance and driving improvements through site KPIs and action plans.
  • Supporting Management of Change (MOC), safety reviews and the development of safe working procedures.
  • Supporting environmental compliance, including waste and wastewater activities.

What we are looking for:

  • Higher Diploma in Safety, Health and Welfare at Work or equivalent.
  • Previous experience in an EHS / Health & Safety role within a manufacturing or regulated environment.
  • Proven experience with Permit to Work / Safe Work Permit systems is essential.
  • Experience managing and coordinating third-party contractors on a manufacturing site.
  • Strong knowledge of risk assessments, method statements and safe systems of work.
  • Experience within a GMP or similarly regulated environment would be advantageous.
  • Strong communication, organisational and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices and hold others accountable.

What is on offer:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Comprehensive benefits package.
  • Monday to Friday, days-only role.
  • Excellent career development opportunities.
  • Long-term opportunity with a well-established manufacturing organisation.
  • A key role working closely with the EHS Manager and wider site teams.

If you are an experienced EHS Coordinator / Health & Safety professional with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience, and are looking for a Monday to Friday, days-only opportunity in Little Island, Cork, apply today with your CV.
